rules.name: SQL Injection in product search (q parameter)

shortDescription.text: SQL Injection in product search (q parameter)

fullDescription.text: The `q` query parameter of GET /rest/products/search is concatenated into a SQL statement without parameterisation. A single quote followed by a UNION SELECT returns rows from the users table.

help.text:
The `q` query parameter of GET /rest/products/search is concatenated into a SQL statement without parameterisation. A single quote followed by a UNION SELECT returns rows from the users table.

An unauthenticated attacker can read arbitrary database content, including credential hashes of every account.

Use parameterised queries / prepared statements for every database access, validate `q` against an allow-list pattern, and stop returning raw database errors to clients.

rules.name: Reflected XSS in search results page

shortDescription.text: Reflected XSS in search results page

fullDescription.text: The `q` value is echoed into the search results HTML without output encoding, so a crafted link executes attacker-controlled script in the victim's browser.

help.text:
The `q` value is echoed into the search results HTML without output encoding, so a crafted link executes attacker-controlled script in the victim's browser.

Session token theft and account takeover for any user who opens a malicious link.

Contextually encode all reflected values, adopt a strict Content-Security-Policy, and mark session cookies HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict.

rules.name: Server banner discloses framework and version

shortDescription.text: Server banner discloses framework and version

fullDescription.text: Responses expose `X-Powered-By: Express` and verbose stack traces on malformed requests, easing targeted exploitation.

help.text:
Responses expose `X-Powered-By: Express` and verbose stack traces on malformed requests, easing targeted exploitation.

Attackers can fingerprint the stack and prioritise known framework weaknesses.

Remove the X-Powered-By header, return generic error bodies, and disable stack traces outside development.

message.text:
SQL Injection in product search (q parameter)

The `q` query parameter of GET /rest/products/search is concatenated into a SQL statement without parameterisation. A single quote followed by a UNION SELECT returns rows from the users table.

errow.impact: An unauthenticated attacker can read arbitrary database content, including credential hashes of every account.
errow.technical_analysis: Response time differential (SLEEP) and boolean-based probes confirmed injection into a string context; UNION column count is 9. The back-end is SQLite and the error message leaks the failing query.
errow.remediation_steps: Use parameterised queries / prepared statements for every database access, validate `q` against an allow-list pattern, and stop returning raw database errors to clients.
errow.counterevidence: No WAF or input filter was observed between the client and the application.
errow.severity_change_conditions: Severity drops to medium if the database account is read-only and holds no credential data.
errow.fix_verification: Re-run the UNION and boolean probes after deploying parameterised queries; both must return an empty result set.

poc.description: GET /rest/products/search?q=')) UNION SELECT id,email,password,4,5,6,7,8,9 FROM Users-- returns user rows in the product list.

message.text:
Reflected XSS in search results page

The `q` value is echoed into the search results HTML without output encoding, so a crafted link executes attacker-controlled script in the victim's browser.

errow.impact: Session token theft and account takeover for any user who opens a malicious link.
errow.technical_analysis: The payload `<iframe src="javascript:alert(1)">` is rendered unescaped inside the results header; the session cookie is not HttpOnly.
errow.remediation_steps: Contextually encode all reflected values, adopt a strict Content-Security-Policy, and mark session cookies HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict.
errow.counterevidence: No CSP header or output encoding was present on the response.
errow.severity_change_conditions: Severity rises to high if the session cookie is readable from script and tokens grant administrative access.

poc.description: Open /#/search?q=<iframe src="javascript:alert(1)"> in a browser; the alert fires.

message.text:
Server banner discloses framework and version

Responses expose `X-Powered-By: Express` and verbose stack traces on malformed requests, easing targeted exploitation.

errow.impact: Attackers can fingerprint the stack and prioritise known framework weaknesses.
errow.technical_analysis: A malformed JSON body to /api/Challenges returns a full Express stack trace including file system paths.
errow.remediation_steps: Remove the X-Powered-By header, return generic error bodies, and disable stack traces outside development.
errow.confidence_rationale: Observed on one endpoint only; other routes were not fuzzed for error handling.
